newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates ease on added liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates ease on added liquidity.

text.p: * Helped by Central Bank's dollar purchases
Philippine interbank call loan rates eased on Thursday after three days of tighness due to added liquidity arising from the Central Bank's purchases of dollars and maturing T-bills, traders said.
The average rate fell to 12.03125 percent from 13.03125.
"Big banks were lenders," a trader from a big bank said.
Done rates ranged from 14.0833 to 11.0625 percent, with volume higher at 27.356 billion from 26.465 billion pesos.
Dealers said the Central Bank was a net buyer of dollars since Monday, which effectively released more pesos out of its vaults.
Moreover, an estimated 1.2 billion pesos had gone back to banks from maturing Treasury bills, one trader said.

The secondary market of T-bills generated more sellers than buyers since banks wanted to remain liquid during the Nov 22 to 26 holidays in view of the summit meeting of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation, traders said.
Banks will remain open on Friday, Monday and Tuesday but the regular treasury bills auction on Monday will not be held.
Peso dollar trading on the Philippine Dealing System will also be closed.
The three-month bills were given an offer rate of 11.55 to 11.75 percent; the six months at 12.15 to 12.35; and the one year at 12.55 to 12.675, traders said.
